title: "Titan.jl"
subtitle: "Implicit Radiation Hydrodynamics for the First Stars, Supermassive Seeds & Primordial Transients"
toc: false
---

`Titan.jl` is a pure-Julia, fully implicit 1D moving-mesh radiation-hydrodynamics (RHD) and primordial astrophysics suite descended from Gehmeyr & Mihalas's `TITAN` [@gehmeyr1994]. Within a single unified codebase—pairing exact automatic-differentiation Jacobians, smooth $C^2$ thermodynamics (`FreeEnergyEOS`, `StellarEOS`), zero-metallicity and molecular opacities (`StellarOpacity`, `ContinuumOpacity`, ExoMol `H2Lines`), coupled primordial chemistry (`ChemNet`, `UnifiedNonLTE`), 35-group ionizing & Lyman–Werner radiation transport (`IonRay`), $l$-resolved nebular line transfer (`ModelAtom`, `SpecFull`), nuclear burning (`NucNet`), and 1PN/TOV general relativity (`GR_CORR`)—`Titan.jl` reproduces **17 landmark astrophysics papers** across 22 orders of magnitude in density and 10 decades in mass.

## How to Use the Interactive Explorer

Every figure in the [Interactive Laboratory](app/index.html) and embedded chapter widgets shares one consistent, framework-free visualization engine (`app/js/viz/plot.js`):

- **Click-to-highlight across linked graphs:** clicking any shell, mass, density, time, or spectral line on one plot highlights the exact matching physical state across all companion plots and tables.
- **User-controlled axes & zoom:** scroll over a plot to zoom both axes (or over an axis strip to zoom that axis alone), drag to pan, toggle `lin`/`log` independently on $x$ and $y$, type exact `min`–`max` bounds, or double-click / click `reset` to restore defaults.
- **Publication-ready downloads:** every plot toolbar includes one-click **`svg`** (standalone vector graphic), **`png`** (2× high-DPI bitmap), and **`csv`** (full-precision plotted data) export.

::: {.callout-note title="How to read provenance badges in Part III (Quasi-Stars)"}
In the Quasi-Star deep-dive chapters (@sec-mesa-quest through @sec-spectra), a Rust/WebAssembly numerical core evaluates the steady-envelope equations live in the browser: a superscript ⟨name⟩ links to the generated Rust API docs, a ✓ badge links to the automated test pinning a number, and **[computed] / [tested] / [estimate] / [interpretation]** tags classify each statement. Companion resources: [*What a fed quasi-star looks like*](spectra/index.html) and [the slide talk](talk/index.html).
:::
